SignedOut.title: Signed out
SignedOut.notAdminExplanation: This account can't administer Kale (it doesn't hold auth.Admin); it has been signed out.
SignedOut.sessionEndedExplanation: It was stopped by an administrator, it expired or couldn't be renewed, or you signed in somewhere else. Sign in again to continue.

NotAdmin.title: Not allowed
NotAdmin.explanation: This account can't administer Kale (it doesn't hold auth.Admin).

Forms.invalid: AuthService refused the change; check the values.
Forms.notFound: It no longer exists (perhaps removed in another tab). Reload the page.
Forms.secretShownOnce: Copy it now: it is shown only this once (AuthService keeps only its hash). Store it as the application's Podman secret.

request.field-required: The request is missing “{field}” (true or false).
request.sort-unknown: The list can't be sorted by “{sort}”.
request.concurrent-change: Someone else changed the same data at the same moment, so nothing was saved. Try again.

application.key-invalid: “{key}” can't be a key: 2-63 lowercase letters, digits or dashes, starting with a letter.
application.key-taken: An application with the key “{key}” already exists.
application.name-too-long: The name can be at most {max} characters.
application.address-missing: One of the return addresses is empty.
application.address-has-fragment: “{address}” can't be used: a return address can't have a fragment (#…).
application.address-not-https: “{address}” can't be used: enter a full https address (plain http only for localhost).
application.auth-addresses-fixed: The admin UI's return addresses are set when Kale is set up; they can't be changed here.
application.auth-cannot-be-deactivated: Kale's own application (auth) can't be deactivated: the admin UI depends on it.
application.auth-no-desktop-sign-in: Kale's own application (auth) can't have desktop sign-in.
application.auth-cannot-be-deleted: Kale's own application (auth) can't be deleted: the admin UI depends on it.
application.still-active: Deactivate the application ({key}) before deleting it.

role.name-required: Enter a name for the role.
role.name-too-long: A role name can be at most {max} characters.
role.description-too-long: A role description can be at most {max} characters.
role.name-taken: This application already has a role named “{name}”.
role.operations-unknown: Not a current operation of this application: {operations}.

group.name-required: Enter a name for the group.
group.name-too-long: A group name can be at most {max} characters.
group.description-too-long: A group description can be at most {max} characters.
group.name-taken: There is already a group named “{name}”.

admin.last-admin: That would leave nobody who can administer Kale: no other active user would hold auth.Admin.

user.display-name-too-long: A display name can be at most {max} characters.
user.user-name-too-long: A user name can be at most {max} characters.
user.user-name-invalid: “{userName}” can't be a user name: use only English letters, digits and - . _ @ +
user.user-name-taken: The user name “{userName}” is already taken.
user.cannot-delete-self: You can't delete your own account; another administrator can.

access.default-role-not-in-application: The default role must be one of this application's roles.

password.too-short: The password must be at least {min} characters long.
password.needs-symbol: The password needs at least one character that isn't a letter or a digit.
password.needs-digit: The password needs at least one digit (0-9).
password.needs-lowercase: The password needs at least one lowercase letter (a-z).
password.needs-uppercase: The password needs at least one uppercase letter (A-Z).
password.needs-unique-chars: The password needs at least {count} different characters.

Applications.title: Applications
Applications.explanation: The applications that sign their users in with Kale. Each registers its own operations; roles grant them.
Applications.newExplanation: Kale makes its client secret and shows it once.
Applications.keyHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Can't be changed later.
Applications.name: Name
Applications.onePerLine: One address per line; https (http only for localhost). Leave empty for an API without a web front end.
Applications.confirmRotate: Give {key} a new client secret? The current one keeps working for a while, so you can redeploy the application; tick the box to stop it at once.
Applications.confirmDeactivate: Deactivate {key}? Nobody can sign in to it, and its open sessions end.
Applications.adminUiSecret: The admin UI's own secret: replace it with the admin UI's Podman secret, not here.
Applications.alwaysActive: Kale itself (the admin UI's application) is always active: nobody could administer Kale otherwise.
Applications.confirmRotateReplacingOld: Give {key} a new client secret? Only one old secret is kept: the old one that works until {until} stops at once, and the current one becomes the old one.
Applications.retireOldAtOnce: Stop the current secret at once (e.g. it leaked)
Applications.oldSecretWorksUntil: The old secret still works until {until}. Retire it once every instance runs with the new one.
Applications.confirmRetireOld: Retire the old client secret of {key}? Instances still using it can no longer sign users in or call Kale.

Application.name: Name
Application.onePerLine: One address per line; https (http only for localhost, in local development).
Application.keyIsPermanent: The key can't change: it is the application's client id, its tokens' audience and its operations' prefix.
Application.adminUiAddresses: This is the admin UI itself: its return addresses are set when Kale is set up (admin bootstrap) and can't be changed.
Application.secretExplanation: The application uses it to sign users in and to call Kale. Kale keeps only its hash. After a new secret, the old one keeps working for a while, so running instances can be redeployed.
Application.activeExplanation: Users with access can sign in.
Application.inactiveExplanation: Nobody can sign in, and its sessions aren't accepted.
Application.confirmDelete: Delete {key} for good? Its roles, operations, users' access to it and its client secrets are removed, and its open sessions stop. Users and groups stay. This can't be undone.
Application.desktopOffExplanation: Off: only the web application signs users in. On, desktop apps (e.g. WPF) sign users in through the system browser, without a client secret.
Application.desktopOnExplanation: Desktop apps sign users in through the system browser, without a client secret. A user has one session per application: signing in on the desktop ends their web session, and the other way round.
Application.confirmDesktopOff: Turn off desktop sign-in for {key}? Signed-in desktop users can't renew their sign-in and must sign in again once it's back on.
Application.noDesktopForAdminUi: The admin UI is a web application: it has no desktop sign-in.

Error.title: Something went wrong
Error.explanation: The page couldn't be loaded or the change couldn't be made. AuthService may be unreachable.

Roles.title: Roles
Roles.explanation: A role grants operations of this application. Users get roles directly or through groups.
Roles.name: Name
Roles.operationsExplanation: The application registers these itself at startup; they can't be added here.
Roles.obsolete: Obsolete: no longer registered by the application
Roles.noOperations: The application hasn't registered any operations yet (it does at startup).

Role.operationsExplanation: Everyone with this role can do these (and what they imply). Changes apply at once, also to users signed in now.
Role.obsolete: Obsolete: no longer registered; dropped at the next change
Role.noOperations: This role grants no operations yet.
Role.confirmRemove: Remove {operation} from {name}? Everyone with this role loses it at once.
Role.addExplanation: Everyone with this role gains them at once.
Role.nothingToAdd: The role already holds every current operation.
Role.obsoleteDropped: The role also holds obsolete operations; they are dropped with this change: {operations}
Role.name: Name
Role.confirmDelete: Delete the role {name}? Its open sessions stop at once, and users and groups lose it.

Users.title: Users
Users.explanation: Accounts that sign in with Kale. A user needs access to an application and a role in it.
Users.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. Give it to the user through a safe channel.

User.disabledExplanation: can't sign in; their sessions were stopped
User.detailsHint: A correction keeps the user signed in; they sign in with the new user name from now on.
User.confirmDelete: Delete {userName} for good? Their sessions stop at once, and their access, roles and group memberships are removed. This can't be undone; to only stop them signing in, disable the user instead.
User.confirmDisable: Disable {userName}? All their sessions stop at once and they can't sign in.
User.applicationsHint: Signing in to an application needs active access to it and a role (direct or through a group). A new role gives access when there was none; access turned off stays off.
User.noApplications: No access to any application yet.
User.confirmAccess: Save the access to {key}? Making it inactive stops their sessions there at once.
User.rolesHint: Roles from groups are on the groups.
User.assignExplanation: The user holds them at once, and gets access to their applications where they had none (access turned off stays off).
User.noRolesLeft: The user already holds every role directly.
User.confirmUnassign: Remove the role {role} ({key})? Their sessions with it stop, unless a group still grants it.
User.groupsHint: The user holds every role of these groups.
User.passwordHint: Setting a new one also ends a lockout. The user is signed out of every application and signs in again with it.
User.confirmPassword: Set a new password for {userName}? They are signed out of every application at once.
User.twoFactorHint: Users turn it on themselves on Kale's own pages, with an authenticator app. A reset is for a lost phone: it turns it off and signs them out of every application.
User.confirmResetTwoFactor: Turn off two-step sign-in for {userName}? They are signed out of every application at once and can set it up again on their account page.
User.lockedOutUntil: Locked out until {time} after too many wrong passwords or codes

Groups.title: Groups
Groups.explanation: Members of a group hold all of its roles (groups don't nest).
Groups.name: Name

Group.name: Name
Group.confirmDelete: Delete the group {name}? Its members lose its roles, and their sessions with those roles stop (unless they still hold them another way).
Group.confirmRemoveMember: Remove {userName} from the group? Their sessions with the group's roles stop (unless they still hold them another way).
Group.addMembersExplanation: They hold the group's roles at once, and get access to their applications where they had none (access turned off stays off).
Group.noUsersLeft: Every user is already a member.
Group.rolesHint: Every member holds these roles. Members get access to their applications when they join or a role is added, unless their access was turned off (on the user's page).
Group.confirmRemoveRole: Remove the role {role} ({key}) from the group? Members' sessions with it stop (unless they still hold it another way).
Group.addRolesExplanation: Every member holds them at once, and gets access to their applications where they had none (access turned off stays off).
Group.noRolesLeft: The group already holds every role.

Sessions.title: Open sessions
Sessions.explanation: Signed in and not yet ended or expired. Times are in {timeZone}.
Sessions.confirmStop: Stop this session of {userName} in {key}? The application refuses it at once; they have to sign in again.

TestToken.title: Test token
TestToken.explanation: A user's access token to an application, to try your API before it has a sign-in page. Kale refuses this outside development.
TestToken.sideEffect: It's a real sign-in of that user (under the normal rules: active user, access and role), so it ends their other session in that application.
TestToken.roleHint: A role of the chosen application.
TestToken.tokenNote: Shown only here; get a new one when it expires.
TestToken.try: Call your API with it, for example:
